Helen Oakley Dance has been involved in jazz since the 1930s. Born in Toronto in 1913, she moved to Chicago as a young woman to be closer to the hot jazz of the decade. Through her own initiative, she recorded Paul Mares, Jabbo Smith and Jess Stacey, and staged concerts with Count Basie and Benny Goodman. It was at one of these concerts that Benny was brought together with pianist Teddy Wilson, setting the stage for one of the most famous trios in jazz history. Helen enjoyed a long and fruitful relationship with Duke Ellington and produced numerous small group recordings with Duke and members of his orchestra for the Variety label. She has written for Down Beat, The Saturday Review and The Music Journal, and in 1987 she authored Stormy Monday, The T-Bone Walker Story. Helen married Stanley Dance in 1947. Together they have become a part of jazz history by documenting priceless stories from the Golden Age of Jazz.
Helen and Stanley currently reside in Vista, California. Helen was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 12, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are in San Diego filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I am honored to have Helen Oakley Dance as my guest, author and jazz lover. Thanks so much for being with me.
